text:
ConocoPhillips edged down 0.43% today to $141.73, a small pullback after a strong two-week rally of 11.55%. The decline likely reflects profit-taking following yesterday's jump to $142.34, especially as oil prices softened—U.S. crude fell near $98 on Thursday as traders assessed Iran's attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and digested new supply data from the International Energy Agency. Even with today's small retreat, the stock remains well above where it started the period, boosted by the broader oil strength that has defined the past two weeks.

The underlying tailwind for the rally has been a tightening physical oil market: tanker rates have surged enough that the real cost to deliver oil is roughly $38 per barrel higher than benchmark prices suggest, and U.S. diesel prices have hit record highs, drawing attention to global refining bottlenecks. That structural supply tightness has supported oil prices even as geopolitical tensions around Iran have created near-term volatility rather than sustained gains.
